To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the RC of graphene/metal contacts is strongly dependent on the metal type.
the contact resistance of graphene is strongly dependent on the choice of metal and that noble metals show the lowest contact resistance.
the RC of graphene/metal contacts is strongly dependent on the work function of the metal and that annealing the contacts can improve the contact resistance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of contact resistance in graphene/metal junctions.
the electrical characterization of graphene/metal contacts.
the electrical properties of graphene and graphene based devices.

the RC of graphene/metal contacts can be reduced by using noble metals.
the RC values for noble metals are significantly lower than the values for non-noble metals.
the noble metals are superior to other metals for graphene contacts, and that high temperature anneal is beneficial to reduce RC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
noble metal contacts show lower RC values than the other metals.
noble metals are the best choices for graphene contacts.
the noble metals show lower resistance and the annealing process improves the contact resistance for all metals.

noble metals are better candidates for graphene contacts.
